documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MRA in December showed the coils holding; next one in 3 years.
A1c 7.3. Fasting 120s to 140s, no lows since she stopped skipping breakfast.
Home BP log 128 to 138 over low 80s.
No new symptoms. Trigeminal pain has not returned in years; she asks whether she could ever come off carbamazepine. Reasonable question for neurology; she'll raise it if she sees them, otherwise no change for now.
Exam: well. Heart and lungs normal. No edema. Feet: intact skin, pulses good, toes numb as before.
Plan: continue all meds. Labs today. June visit.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 60 next month.
Stable year. Oncology NED. LDCT June negative. Eye exam May normal.
Meds unchanged. NKDA. No tobacco.
ROS negative. PHQ-2 0.
Exam: BP at goal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Breasts normal. Abdomen soft. Joints without synovitis. No edema. Neuro: nonfocal; slight right smile asymmetry unchanged. Feet as before.
Flu and COVID given.
Plan: annual labs, mammogram. Colonoscopy due spring 2026, will refer at the next physical. Visit February.

reports.text: Bilateral standard views with tomosynthesis. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion. Stable.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine chronic care visit. Feels well. Garden is the best it's been; out there most mornings before the heat. No headaches, no facial pain, joints fine. Sugars 110s to 140s fasting. Lung CT last month clear, oncology in May clear.
Meds: lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, atorvastatin 40 nightly, levothyroxine 112 mcg, glargine 20 units qhs, MTX 15 mg weekly, prednisone 5, carbamazepine 200 bid, ondansetron prn (hasn't needed it in a long time). NKDA.

O: BP 134/84. Weight steady. Comfortable. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No ankle edema. Feet: pulses 2+, skin intact, numb great toes unchanged.

A/P
1. HTN: acceptable on two drugs.
2. DM2 on basal insulin: A1c, urine albumin today.
3. Hypothyroid: TSH today.
4. Hyperlipidemia: lipids today.
5. RA on MTX/pred: CBC, CMP today.
6. Hx SAH, coiled; hx ovarian ca, NED; TN quiet.
7. Colonoscopy due 2026; referral at the fall physical.
Return in October for physical and vaccines.

documents.title: Your July labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Renee. A1c 7.4, close to where it has been. Kidney function normal (creatinine 0.9) and no protein in the urine (ratio 21). Thyroid 2.2, good. LDL 132, unchanged. Blood counts and liver tests fine for the methotrexate. No changes. See you in October.

documents.title: Glargine pens and carbamazepine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request: insulin glargine pens (20 units nightly) 90-day supply and carbamazepine 200 mg #180. Last visit 7/7, labs current. Approved per protocol.

documents.title: Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called to book the annual physical discussed in July. Left voicemail. Portal reminder sent.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up (visit 11/17/2025)
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Date of visit: 11/17/2025

Routine visit. Joints remain quiet. New since about September: swelling of both ankles by evening and frothy urine. No rash, no fevers. BP 142/88. Trace to 1+ pitting edema at both ankles. Urine dipstick in clinic 3+ protein, no blood.

After more than ten years of active inflammatory arthritis, secondary (AA) amyloidosis is one concern among others; we have referred her urgently to nephrology. Continue methotrexate 15 mg weekly and prednisone 5 mg for now. Please let us know of any kidney function results.

documents.title: Nephrology consultation (visit 12/10/2025)
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology group
Date of visit: 12/10/2025

Referred by rheumatology for proteinuria. Ms. Duffy is a 62-year-old woman with seropositive RA treated with methotrexate and low-dose prednisone for about a decade, hypertension, type 2 diabetes on basal insulin, hypothyroidism, a remote ovarian carcinoma in remission and a coiled cerebral aneurysm. Over three months she has become more tired, her legs swell, and her urine foams.

Meds: lisinopril 10, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5, atorvastatin 40, levothyroxine 112 mcg, insulin glargine 20 units, ondansetron as needed, carbamazepine 200 twice daily. (Methotrexate and prednisone confirmed with patient.) NKDA.

BP 145/90. Pitting edema of both legs to the knees. Lungs clear.

Data: serum albumin 2.8 g/dL; creatinine 1.2 mg/dL; 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g; urine sediment without cells or casts; total cholesterol 260 mg/dL. Serum protein electrophoresis and serum free light chains: no monoclonal protein.

Assessment: nephrotic syndrome with a bland sediment and mildly reduced filtration. In the setting of long-standing RA, AA amyloidosis is the leading concern; diabetic nephropathy would be unusual with normal albuminuria in July.

Plan: percutaneous renal biopsy next week. Furosemide 40 mg daily for edema; continue lisinopril. Salt restriction. Repeat labs after biopsy.

reports.text: Specimen: kidney, left, percutaneous needle biopsy (2 cores, 24 glomeruli). Light microscopy: glomeruli with mesangial and capillary wall expansion by amorphous eosinophilic material that is pale on PAS and silver stains; similar deposits in arteriolar walls and focal interstitium. Congo red stain: deposits are congophilic and show apple-green birefringence under polarized light. Immunofluorescence: no significant immunoglobulin or complement staining; kappa and lambda equal. Electron microscopy: randomly arranged non-branching fibrils, 8 to 10 nm. Typing by mass spectrometry sent.

documents.title: Renal biopsy pathology
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Renal biopsy report from nephrology received and scanned; routed to PCP.

documents.title: Nephrology letter: amyloid typing (01/12/2026)
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology group
Date: 01/12/2026

Mass spectrometry on the renal biopsy identifies serum amyloid A protein: AA amyloidosis, which we attribute to her long-standing rheumatoid arthritis. No evidence of AL disease.

I have spoken with her rheumatologist. Treatment centers on suppressing inflammation; with falling filtration, methotrexate should be replaced. Creatinine today 1.6 mg/dL. Furosemide continues. We will follow monthly.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel her physical tomorrow. She has nephrology and rheumatology appointments this month and asked to wait until things settle. Will call back to rebook.

documents.title: Rheumatology visit (02/09/2026)
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Date of visit: 02/09/2026

AA amyloidosis confirmed on renal biopsy. Methotrexate stopped today because of declining kidney function. QuantiFERON-TB Gold negative and hepatitis B surface antigen negative. Starting tocilizumab 162 mg subcutaneously every week; injection teaching done. Prednisone 5 mg continues. Live vaccines to be avoided. CBC and liver tests monthly through our office for three months.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up (03/23/2026)
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology group
Date: 03/23/2026

Swelling better on furosemide, now below the mid-shin. Creatinine 2.3 mg/dL, albumin 2.6 g/dL. On tocilizumab since February. Her kidney function is declining faster than we hoped. We began dialysis education today and discussed modality and access; she leans toward in-center hemodialysis. Labs every 2 weeks.

documents.title: Kidney update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just letting you know where things stand. The kidney doctors say I will probably need dialysis this year because of the amyloid. I'm taking the classes. I know I owe you a physical, I'll book once I know my schedule. Please keep my prescriptions going in the meantime.

documents.title: RE: Kidney update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, Renee, I'm sorry this is happening. I've read the nephrology letters. Refills will keep coming. Call or text anytime, and when your dialysis days are set, we'll find a visit time that works around them.

documents.title: Nephrology: start of hemodialysis (05/19/2026)
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology group
Date: 05/19/2026

Over the past two weeks she developed nausea, poor appetite and fatigue. Labs 05/18: creatinine 5.8 mg/dL, BUN 82 mg/dL, potassium 5.4 mmol/L, bicarbonate 18 mmol/L, hemoglobin 9.3 g/dL, phosphorus 6.4 mg/dL.

Assessment: end-stage kidney disease from AA amyloidosis.

A right internal jugular tunneled hemodialysis catheter was placed today by interventional radiology under ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance without complication; tip at the cavoatrial junction. First hemodialysis session today, then in-center three times weekly (Mon/Wed/Fri). Hydrochlorothiazide stopped. Furosemide continues for residual urine output. Anemia and mineral management to start at the dialysis unit.

documents.title: Tunneled dialysis catheter placement (05/19/2026)
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Procedure: placement of right internal jugular tunneled cuffed hemodialysis catheter.
Ultrasound-guided venous access; fluoroscopic confirmation of tip at the cavoatrial junction. Moderate sedation. No complications. Catheter flushed and locked with heparin. Ready for use.

documents.title: Dialysis unit monthly summary (June 2026)
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient dialysis unit, monthly summary dated 06/22/2026

In-center hemodialysis three times weekly via right IJ tunneled catheter since 05/19/2026. Tolerating treatments.

Started this month: sevelamer carbonate 800 mg three times daily with meals; epoetin alfa 4000 units IV with each session.

Current medications per unit: lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, levothyroxine 112 mcg daily, insulin glargine 20 units at bedtime, prednisone 5 mg daily, carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily, ondansetron 4 mg every 8 hours as needed, furosemide 40 mg daily, tocilizumab 162 mg weekly, sevelamer, epoetin alfa. Hydrochlorothiazide discontinued 05/19. Methotrexate discontinued 02/09.

Allergies: none known.

Vascular access planning discussed with the patient.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: I'm on dialysis Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings now, done by noon. Could I come in on a Monday afternoon in September? I'd like to go over everything with you.

documents.body: You're booked Monday 9/14 at 2:30 with your doctor, a 40-minute visit. Please bring your dialysis unit medication list.
